Area.evidence_source: In addition to what they felt was mislabeling and disrespectful staff attitudes, some participants attributed their difficulty in receiving assistance with mental health issues to a lack of time to conduct a proper assessment or to speak about problems. In the context of an inpatient setting, many participants said they saw a psychiatrist for several minutes a day and that nurses often did not speak with them. Many felt that they sat on the ward for days and were not given the opportunity to speak with nurses or psychiatrists about their problems or to do anything else productive. In family practices, appointments were said to be too short to be productive or therapeutic. "The nurses never left the nurse's station, so there was no interaction . . . which I think is very important that you have nurses on the floor and you can go to any nurse, not necessarily your primary nurse, or your secondary nurse, and there was never a doctor on the floor . . . so that left me feeling pretty hopeless and that's when I cut myself and acted out in an outward sort of way . . ." (18:844)
